html:
The Añuu, also called Paraujano, are an Arawakan-speaking people of the shores and lagoons of Lake Maracaibo in northwestern Venezuela. They are known for their villages of houses on stilts over the water.

In 1499 the Spanish expedition of Alonso de Ojeda, with Amerigo Vespucci aboard, sailed into the lake and saw such stilt villages. They were reminded of Venice and called the land Venezuela, "little Venice". The Añuu still live in stilt houses in the Sinamaica Lagoon. Their language, close to that of the Wayuu of the Guajira, is now spoken by very few people.
